parts.title: The Festival
parts.text: Every year, the small village held a **jubilant** festival, full of cheering and laughter, that filled the streets with music and dancing. This year, a great storm had swept through and left everyone feeling low. The mayor knew she had to act fast to **soothe** the villagers' worries and lift the community's spirits before festival day arrived.

parts.title: The Preparation
parts.text: She walked through the village with clear **intent**: she was going to make this the best festival yet. Her **approach** was simple — talk to every neighbor and ask them to help decorate. The decorations were **vibrant**, with bold colors bursting from every window and doorway. Children painted a **mammoth** mural of suns and waves along the town wall, taller than any grown-up.

parts.title: The Celebration
parts.text: When festival day came, the cheerful **clamor** of the crowd filled the streets as the parade began. A young girl who had always been quiet and **meek** stood up and recited a poem with a clear, loud voice. She had used her **wit** to write something funny and touching. The mayor stood **poised** and calm, then gave a nod to start the fireworks right on time. The storm had arrived with **fury**, but the festival proved the village could not be broken. Everyone would **approve** of how the day turned out.

parts.title: The Memory
parts.text: That night, the whole village sat under the stars and shared stories. The mayor smiled and said the best festivals are not the ones with the most money — they are the ones where everyone comes together. The children promised to help decorate again next year, and the festival grew even stronger.

definitions.meaning1: Extreme anger or rage. Example: The giant flew into a fury when he found his gold had been stolen.

definitions.meaning2: Paying very close attention. Example: The cat watched the mouse with intent eyes.

definitions.meaning1: Extremely large; huge. Example: A mammoth truck blocked the whole road.
definitions.meaning2: A large, hairy animal like an elephant that lived long ago. Example: Mammoths walked the Earth thousands of years ago.

definitions.meaning1: Bright, strong, and full of energy. Example: The flowers in the garden were vibrant, with bright yellows and deep reds.

definitions.meaning1: The ability to say things that are clever and funny. Example: Her quick wit made everyone laugh during the long car ride.

definitions.meaning1: A way of dealing with something. Example: The team had to decide on the best approach for solving the problem.
definitions.meaning2: To move closer to something. Example: She began to approach the podium slowly, nervous about her speech.

definitions.meaning1: To agree with or accept something. Example: The principal was happy to approve the new lunch menu.
definitions.meaning2: To have a good opinion of something. Example: Her parents did not approve of staying up past midnight.

definitions.meaning1: A loud, confused noise, often made by many people at once. Example: The clamor of the crowd filled the stadium.
definitions.meaning2: To demand something loudly. Example: Fans clamor for tickets to the big game.

definitions.meaning1: Quiet, gentle, and not wanting to argue. Example: The meek child gave a soft nod and stepped aside.

definitions.meaning1: Feeling or showing great joy, especially because of a success. Example: The jubilant fans cheered when their team won the game.

definitions.meaning1: Balanced and ready; calm and confident. Example: The diver stood poised at the end of the board.
definitions.meaning2: Calm and sure of yourself. Example: The poised speaker answered every question without a worry.

definitions.meaning1: To calm someone or ease a worry or pain. Example: She sang softly to soothe the crying baby.
definitions.meaning2: To make pain or an itch feel better. Example: Cool aloe gel can soothe a sunburn.
